translator: Claude (AI), draft, not reviewed by a Hittitologist
intro: Manuscript B of Muršili II's so-called Second Plague Prayer, addressed to the Storm-god of Ḫatti (CTH 378.2; Singer no. 11), joined from KBo 55.25 + KUB 14.11 + DAAM 5.78. It preserves the complaint about twenty years of plague, the story of the broken oath with Egypt, the Egyptian campaign and the plague brought home by the prisoners, the oracle findings about the oath and the Mala River offering, Muršili's confession of his father's sin, and his closing call for dreams, oracles and incubation to reveal any other cause.

paras.en: […] and […] very […]. And in the time of [my father …] and [since I] be[came] priest […], in (my) time they keep [dying]. [Th]is [is] the twentieth year th[at] people have been dy[ing in the land of Ḫatti], [and] the plague [has] no[t at a]ll come to an end in the land of Ḫatti. [And] I […] [cannot master] the [a]gitation […], and the anguish of (my) [bo]dy […] I [can no longer] master.

[…] when I celebrated […], [I attended to all the go]ds; I did not single out [any one] temple. […] I [made (pleas)] to all the gods […] I kept [vow]ing(?): '[…] hear (me) […] the plague [… send away]! Ḫattuša [will] prevail(?). […] keeps dying […] let it be [determin]ed(?) […]' [Break.] And since the men of Ḫatti and the men of Egypt had been put under oath by the Storm-god of Ḫatti, the men of Ḫatti proceeded to turn away first(?): the men of Ḫatti promptly broke the oath of the gods. My father sent troops and chariotry, and they attacked the border of the land of Egypt, the land of Amka. And when the men of Egypt became afraid, they then sent (envoys), and they came and asked my father outright for his son for kingship. But when my father gave them his son, as they were leading him away, they killed him. My father became enraged, went into the land of Egypt and attacked the land of Egypt, and the troops and chariotry of Egypt […]. And then too the Storm-god of Ḫatti […] exalted my father by (his) verdict, and he defeated the troops and chariotry of the land of Egypt and struck them down. When they brought back to the land of Ḫatti the captured men whom they had seized, a plague broke out among the prisoners, and they began to die.

When they brought the prisoners into the land of Ḫatti, the prisoners brought the plague into the land of Ḫatti, and from that day on there has been dying in Ḫatti. When I found that tablet concerning the land of Egypt, I inquired about it through the god (by oracle): 'That matter which was brought about [by] the Storm-god of Ḫatti — that [the men of E]gypt and the men of Ḫatti had been put under oath [by] the Storm-god of Ḫatti; that the [Damnašša]ra deities (were) in the temple of [the Storm-god …]; but that the men of Ḫatti […] transgressed [the wo]rd — […] (has it become a cause of) anger to the Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord?' […] It was confirmed (by oracle).
[… of the Mal]a [River], I inquired by oracle concerning the plague […] [the Storm-god] of Ḫatti […] [Break.] […] hear […] let the plague come [to an end]!

[…] I inquired [by or]acle, […] the matters which were confirmed […] I am resolving(?) […] I am making restitution (for them). […] [the oath] of the gods which [was confirmed] concerning the plague […] to the Storm-god of Ḫatti […] I have offered; I have offered (it) up(?) before (you). To you, the Storm-god of Ḫatti, […] and the offering to them(?) […]. But as for the offering to the Mala River which was confirmed for me [concerning the plague]: look, since I am going [to the Ma]la River, Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord, (and) gods, my lords, allow me the offering to the Mala River! Let me perform the offering to the Mala River, and let me carry it out properly, for the matter of the plague on account of which I am performing it. Gods, my lords, take pity on me, and let the plague in the land of Ḫatti abate!

Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord, (and) gods, my lords: it keeps happening — people do sin. My father too sinned, and he transgressed the word of [the Storm-god …]. But I did not […] sin. It happens (thus) […]: the sin of the father comes upon his son; and upon me too the si[n] of my father has come. Look, I have now confessed it before the Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord, (and) the gods, my lords: it is so, we did it. And since I have confessed the sin of my father, let the soul of the Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord, and of the gods, my lords, be appeased again! Take pity on me again, and send the plague away from the land of Ḫatti again! And these few bread-offerers(?) and libation pourers who are left — let them not die!
Look, I am now making a plea to the Storm-god, my lord, concerning the plague. Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord, hear me and keep me alive!

[…] [to the Storm-god] of Ḫatti, my lord […] […] for (this) reason […] while […] and of the gods […] and the libation pourers [who are left] […] let them not die any more. […] If they keep [dying] for [so]me other (reason), then let me either [see] it [in a dream], or let it be [established] through an oracle, or let a man of god [spe]ak it, or — as I have instructed all the priests — they shall keep sleeping in purity (concerning it). Storm-god of Ḫatti, my lord, keep me alive! Let the gods, my lords, show forth (their) divine providence! Let someone see it in a dream then, and let the [ca]use for which they keep dying be found! […] we shall swing(?) [from the šarp]a- (sense obscure) […] keep (me) alive!
